brief.industry_meta: Shared Electric Micromobility · E-bikes and E-scooters
brief.ticker: Nasdaq: LIME (roadshow live; pricing expected next week)
brief.deck: Lime launched its IPO roadshow on 22 June: 6.96M shares at $24-$26, up to about $181M at a valuation of up to about $1.8B (Renaissance Capital), Nasdaq ticker LIME. A profitable, electric, city-centre mobility brand is about to become public in the cities where Formula E races.
brief.the_case_p1: Lime announced the roadshow on 22 June with pricing expected the following week; Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan lead the books and Uber, holder of 24.4% pre-IPO, has indicated interest in up to $20M of shares. The business on sale is no longer a scooter story: FY2025 revenue was $886.7M, up 29%, with adjusted EBITDA of $218.1M and free cash flow of $103.8M, a third positive year, against a $59.3M net loss driven by debt costs. Proceeds repay a $115M term loan at 10% due in September 2026, which frees the cash flow behind it.
brief.the_case_p2: A newly listed consumer brand needs a public-market story about scale and cities, and Formula E races in Lime's cities. London, where Lime has served more than 400,000 customers, hosts the season finale on 15-16 August; Berlin and Madrid follow in the GEN4 season. No shared-mobility brand has ever raced on the grid, so the first one defines the category.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  Pricing lands next week and the first public-company brand budget is set in July, with the London E-Prix on 15-16 August eight weeks out. Season 13 opens in Jeddah in December with a GEN4 car and a 21-race calendar.
brief.why_team_para: Envision Racing carries Envision Group as title partner with Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact alongside; there is no mobility or consumer-transport partner, so the lane is clean. The team is British-based and built its identity on the Race Against Climate Change, the same car-replacement argument Lime makes to city halls. It is an independent, not an OEM works entry, so a two-wheel brand is a fit rather than a conflict. London is its home race and Lime's largest European market.
brief.value_content: MODE B - halo with hard mechanics. Lime-liveried rider zones and ride credits for ticket holders at the London, Berlin and Madrid E-Prix, team-branded e-bikes in each host city during race week, and a rider-app audience in the tens of millions for Envision's climate content. For the team: a consumer brand that turns a city race into a city-wide campaign, and Uber-backed distribution the roster does not yet have.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official Micromobility Partner. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, Seasons 13-15, the whole first GEN4 cycle. Estimated $1.5-2.5M a year plus in-kind fleet and ride credits. Scope: car and suit placement, host-city activation in Lime cities, app and rider communications, hospitality at London and Berlin.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Ting has run Lime since May 2020, joining in 2018 after four years at Uber including Chief of Staff to its CEO. Path: Joseph Kraus, President; Ann Gugino, CFO since December 2023; Hannah McClellan Richards, COO from June 2026. No chief marketing officer is listed among the executive officers.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Wayne, you are about to list a brand that lives in London, Berlin and Madrid, and Formula E races in all three. No mobility brand has ever been on that grid. 25 minutes after pricing to see how Envision would put Lime in the finale?”
score_cells: Roadshow live 22 Jun; London finale in eight weeks.
Electric, urban, consumer: FE's cities are Lime's.
Listing motive real; no hard external deadline.
MODE B: host-city activation, no engineering use.
risks: A SCOOTER BRAND IN A B2B PADDOCK
Lime is a consumer brand with thin margins after debt; a sponsorship line competes with city-licence costs and fleet capex.
Size the entry at the low end and weight it to in-kind fleet and ride credits, which cost Lime little.
Pricing and the quiet period come before any marketing decision; the window may not open until the first public quarter.
Approach after pricing with a London-finale package that needs only a July decision.
brief.bottom_line: A profitable electric mobility brand listing on Nasdaq this month, an open micromobility lane on every Formula E roster, and a season finale in its biggest European market eight weeks out. Envision Racing is the clean, independent, climate-led home; the deal is small, in-kind heavy and time-bound.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Envision Racing's roster is Envision Group (title), Sand Technologies, Teijin and Genpact. No Formula E team carries a shared-mobility, e-bike or e-scooter partner, so Official Micromobility Partner is a first-of-category designation at a team-partner price.

why_team.label: Climate identity
why_team.text: Envision Racing built its brand on the Race Against Climate Change programme; Lime's pitch to cities is car-trip replacement. The two stories are the same story, told to fans and to city halls.

why_team.label: Independent, not a works team
why_team.text: Six Formula E teams are owned by car makers or two-wheel makers (Jaguar, Nissan, Porsche, Cupra, Citroën, Mahindra, and Yamaha in the Lola entry). An independent team can put a scooter brand on the car without an OEM marketing department objecting.

why_team.label: London is home for both
why_team.text: Envision is British-based and the London E-Prix is its home race. Lime has served more than 400,000 London customers and runs both e-bikes and e-scooters there. A finale activation in August needs only a July decision.

value.label: Race-week mechanics (Mode B)
value.text: Lime rider zones and ticket-holder ride credits at the London, Berlin and Madrid E-Prix; Envision-liveried e-bikes in each host city during race week; push and in-app messaging to riders in those cities. The team gets a city-wide presence for a city race.

value.label: Audience the roster lacks
value.text: Envision's partners are industrial and enterprise brands. Lime brings a consumer audience across about 230 cities and the Uber ecosystem behind its largest shareholder, which is reach the team cannot buy at this price elsewhere.

value.label: Content
value.text: Driver and team commutes on Lime, a season-long 'last mile to the grid' series, and a shared climate-impact scoreboard built from Lime's ride data and the team's Race Against Climate Change reporting.

value.label: What Envision gives back
value.text: Official Micromobility Partner designation, car and race-suit placement, host-city activation rights, hospitality at London and Berlin, and a public-company partner announcement timed to the GEN4 launch in December.

# Lime → Envision Racing — verification log (N° 183, issued for 22 Jun 2026)

Built in-session on 6 Sep 2026 at no API cost, in rebuild mode for the desk row dated 22 Jun 2026. The thin row read "F1, 84/100, no team"; this case re-points it honestly to **Formula E** and **Envision Racing** at **70/100 WARM**. A $1.6B consumer micromobility company whose IPO proceeds repay debt is not an F1 budget; it is a natural Formula E host-city brand.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** investors.li.me, li.me, sec.gov, techcrunch.com, finance.yahoo.com, micromobility.io, stocktitan.net, theorg.com and envision-racing.com were egress-blocked. Every claim was checked against the search summary of the primary page named in the evidence. Treat VERIFIED lines as REPORTED until a person opens the link. Confidence MEDIUM.

## The trigger

Lime's own release of **22 Jun 2026** (Business Wire on the company IR site) launched the roadshow: 6,956,522 shares, 6,679,791 from Lime, $24-$26, Nasdaq Global Select `LIME`, Goldman Sachs / J.P. Morgan leading. Renaissance Capital sized it at up to $181M and up to $1.8B; Reuters counted about $1.66B at the top of the range. Both are given as "about" in the copy. **Outcome after the issue date:** priced 30 Jun at $25.00 (mid-point), trading from 1 Jul; TechCrunch: $167M raised at about $1.66B; IPOScoop: about $174M including selling stockholders. The app page carries this as "Update since issue".

## Financials (S-1, via Dealroom and micromobility.io summaries — REPORTED until the S-1 is opened)

FY2025 revenue $886.7M (+29%), adjusted EBITDA $218.1M (+42%), operating income $70.4M, net loss $59.3M, free cash flow $103.8M. Use of proceeds: repay the $115M senior secured term loan (10%, matures Sep 2026). About 230 cities in 29 countries at 31 Dec 2025. Uber 24.4% pre-IPO, indicated interest up to $20M at the IPO price.

## Decision path

Executive officers in the S-1/A: **Wayne Ting** (CEO and director since May 2020; ex-Uber chief of staff to the CEO), **Joseph Kraus** (President), **Ann Gugino** (CFO since Dec 2023). **Hannah McClellan Richards** joined as COO in June 2026 (Lime management page; HR Today). **No chief marketing officer is listed** among the executive officers, so the sponsorship owner is the CEO; the brief says so. Lime's public leadership page mentions a chief product officer whose name the search summary did not return — not used.

- Ruled out: Lola Yamaha ABT (Yamaha two-wheelers), the six OEM works entries, Mahindra (vehicle maker), DS Penske (DS exit announced), Andretti (open; second choice, US-weighted).
